title: Carthage Ruins
description: The ancient city of Carthage, once the center of the powerful Carthaginian Empire, later became a major Roman city. Visitors can explore the Antonine Baths, the amphitheater, and the ruins that overlook the Mediterranean Sea.

comments.author: Alice Dupont
comments.content: Amazing historical site with a beautiful sea view. The Roman baths are truly impressive!

comments.author: John Smith
comments.content: A must-see if you visit Tunis. Could use more informational signs though.

title: El Jem Amphitheatre
description: Built in the 3rd century, the El Jem Amphitheatre is one of the largest Roman coliseums in the world. It could hold up to 35,000 spectators and is remarkably well-preserved.

comments.author: Sara Ben Ali
comments.content: It feels like stepping back into ancient Rome. Spectacular structure!

comments.author: Marcus Lee
comments.content: Even more impressive than expected. Definitely worth the trip!

title: Dougga
description: Dougga is one of the best-preserved Roman towns in North Africa. The site includes a well-maintained theater, temples, baths, and houses surrounded by green hills.

comments.author: Elena Rossi
comments.content: A quiet and magical site. You can really feel the history here.

comments.author: Tom H.
comments.content: The theater is in great condition. Bring water—it gets hot!

title: Bulla Regia
description: Famous for its underground Roman villas, Bulla Regia offers a rare glimpse into how ancient residents kept cool during the hot summers. Many mosaics are still visible.

comments.author: Amine Gharbi
comments.content: The underground houses are unique! Great place for archaeology lovers.

comments.author: Laura P.
comments.content: Less crowded than other sites, but very interesting.

title: Thuburbo Majus
description: Thuburbo Majus was a prosperous Roman city known for its large forum, temples, and well-planned layout. The site is surrounded by beautiful countryside and olive trees.

comments.author: Nadia K.
comments.content: Very peaceful and open area. Perfect for photos.

comments.author: Hassan M.
comments.content: Nice ruins, though less restored than El Jem or Dougga.

title: Sbeitla (Sufetula)
description: Sbeitla, known in antiquity as Sufetula, features an exceptionally well-preserved Roman forum and temples. It played an important role during the Byzantine and early Islamic periods.

comments.author: Emma Johnson
comments.content: Fantastic ruins, well maintained. You can walk freely everywhere!

comments.author: Rami Trabelsi
comments.content: Very clean site, staff was helpful and friendly.

title: Kerkouane
description: Kerkouane is one of the best-preserved Punic cities in the Mediterranean. Unlike many other ancient towns in Tunisia, it was abandoned and never rebuilt by the Romans, giving a rare insight into Punic urban planning.
